title: Intel’s Earnings Call: Growing Demand, Mounting Challenges
author: Xebec
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Intel’s third-quarter 2026 earnings call highlighted a widening divide between booming demand for data center processors and a weakening PC market. The company reported revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21% year over year, with adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share. Adjusted gross margin reached 44.1%, exceeding management’s guidance.

Data Center and AI revenue climbed 78% to $7.3 billion, reflecting strong demand for server computing. CEO Lip-Bu Tan emphasized expanding Xeon supply as an immediate priority. Meanwhile, Client Computing and Physical AI revenue fell 5% to $8.1 billion, underscoring the uneven conditions across Intel’s major businesses.

During the call, executives attributed PC weakness to higher memory prices, constrained availability and limited customer budgets. CFO David Zinsner said Intel expects the PC market’s unit shipments to decline approximately 12% in 2026 and roughly 10% in 2027. Customers are also reducing inventories, adding pressure to near-term processor purchases.

Manufacturing remained central to the discussion. Intel confirmed the October release of its 14A 0.9 process design kit, an important milestone for prospective foundry customers. However, technology milestones alone will not establish commercial success; investors still need evidence that customer engagement translates into sustained external manufacturing revenue and improving economics.

The outlook was more cautious than the quarter’s headline growth suggested. Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, adjusted earnings of $0.25 per share and adjusted gross margin of 38%. Management also estimated that disruption at its Israeli Fab 28 would reduce quarterly revenue by approximately $300 million.

The call therefore presented a recovery with substantial execution demands. Intel has growing opportunities in AI infrastructure, but converting demand into shipments requires additional manufacturing and packaging capacity. Its ability to balance that investment against PC weakness and foundry losses will shape whether stronger revenue becomes durable profitability over the coming years.
